lines.en: Isabel, somebody has taken the prize roses from the community garden. Who could have done it?
lines.pt: Isabel, alguém levou as rosas premiadas do jardim da comunidade. Quem poderia ter feito isso?

lines.en: It could have been the kids from number nine. They were kicking a ball near the fence yesterday.
lines.pt: Poderiam ter sido as crianças do número nove. Elas chutavam uma bola perto da cerca ontem.

lines.en: But how could they have climbed the gate? It’s locked every evening, and the fence is quite high.
lines.pt: Mas como poderiam ter subido o portão? Ele é trancado toda noite, e a cerca é bem alta.

lines.en: Good point. Somebody must have had a key. The caretaker might have left it open by mistake.
lines.pt: Boa observação. Alguém deve ter tido uma chave. O zelador pode ter deixado aberto por engano.

lines.en: He swears he locked it. Where could the thief have gone afterwards? The street is always busy at night.
lines.pt: Ele jura que trancou. Para onde o ladrão poderia ter ido depois? A rua está sempre movimentada à noite.

lines.en: Perhaps he could have left by car. Our neighbour heard a van near the corner at around midnight.
lines.pt: Talvez ele pudesse ter ido embora de carro. Nossa vizinha ouviu uma van na esquina por volta da meia-noite.

lines.en: A van? Then it can’t have been the children. Why would they have needed one for a few roses?
lines.pt: Uma van? Então não podem ter sido as crianças. Por que precisariam de uma para algumas rosas?

lines.en: Unless they were working for a rival. The competition for the best garden is serious in this area.
lines.pt: A não ser que trabalhassem para um rival. A competição pelo melhor jardim é séria nesta região.

lines.en: Don’t be ridiculous. Who would have wanted to spoil our chance of winning the prize?
lines.pt: Não seja ridículo. Quem iria querer estragar nossa chance de ganhar o prêmio?

lines.en: I don’t know, but look at those footprints in the mud. They must have been made by large boots.
lines.pt: Não sei, mas olhe essas pegadas na lama. Devem ter sido feitas por botas grandes.

lines.en: And they lead to the old shed. Whoever it was might have hidden something there. Shall we have a look?
lines.pt: E elas levam ao velho galpão. Quem quer que tenha sido pode ter escondido algo lá. Vamos dar uma olhada?

facts.label: Perguntas sobre o passado
facts.sub: Quem poderia ter feito isso? Who could have done it? Para outras perguntas: How could they have got in? A ordem é pergunta + could + sujeito + have.

facts.label: Quem poderia ter?
facts.sub: Use Who could have + particípio? para perguntar sobre uma possibilidade passada: Who could have taken it? Você pede hipóteses, não uma resposta exata.

facts.label: How could they have?
facts.sub: Nas perguntas com How, Where, Why, use: palavra de pergunta + could + sujeito + have + particípio. How could they have climbed it? A ordem muda em relação à afirmação.

pages.title: The missing roses in Liverpool · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a cool Sunday morning in Liverpool. The neighbours have a community garden. Every summer they enter their roses in a competition. This morning Ada discovers the flower beds are empty. She calls her neighbour Ben. Together they begin to investigate.

“Ben, somebody has taken the prize roses from the community garden. Who could have done it?” says Ada. “It could have been the kids from number nine. They were kicking a ball near the fence yesterday.” says Ben. “But how could they have climbed the gate? It’s locked every evening, and the fence is quite high.” says Ada.

pages.title: The missing roses in Liverpool · 3/3
paragraphs: “I don’t know, but look at those footprints in the mud. They must have been made by large boots.” says Ben. “And they lead to the old shed. Whoever it was might have hidden something there. Shall we have a look?” says Ada. In the shed they find a muddy coat. Under it, there are two pots with the roses. The caretaker moved them because of the cold. He had forgotten to tell anyone. Ada and Ben carry the pots back. The mystery is solved before lunch.
